note: Per-row and per-checkpoint code_git_sha values are PRESERVED as originally recorded. This record is additive provenance about the relationship between two regimes; it never rewrites which SHA actually generated any row.

controlled_experiment.design: 2x2 isolating code from upstream data: the same date regenerated under BOTH SHAs on one data snapshot, and under the legacy SHA on both data snapshots.
controlled_experiment.detail: 2025-04-20: 6 of 1774 rows differ in exactly one recorded signal, platoon_xwoba (4.5 -> 4.68), all for player 693307 in game 778246. Regenerating the same date under the LEGACY SHA today reproduces 4.68, and pinned-vs-legacy on one snapshot differs in ZERO fields across all 1774 rows. The cause is Statcast revising xwOBA between generation dates, not the code regime. platoon_xwoba is recorded via _sig() for measurement and was explicitly DROPPED from scoring (measured AUC 0.512, 'no separation'), which is consistent with score, predicted_prob and outcome being byte-identical on those same rows.

replay_evidence.row_order_finding: Within-date row order is NOT deterministic across runs of IDENTICAL code (two 2ce95fe9 runs of 2025-04-20 diverged at index 334 with identical row sets). Order is therefore excluded from the equivalence verdict and content identity is enforced order-independently instead.
